lessons.title: Give a Toast at a Group Dinner
lessons.objective: offer a short toast, respond to others' toasts, and keep a group conversation going
lessons.focus: Porter un toast à quelqu'un or à quelque chose is the standard way to give a toast; the person or thing toasted follows à, never pour. Trinquer à notre amitié means to clink glasses to our friendship, and À notre amitié ! is the short spoken toast with the verb dropped. À la santé de tous ! is the reply when everyone raises a glass; tout le monde takes a singular verb: tout le monde lève son verre et répond. Un toast also means a slice of toasted bread, so porter un toast is the phrase that makes the meaning clear. Lever takes è before a silent ending: je lève, ils lèvent, but nous levons. Vous me permettez de dire quelques mots ? asks the whole table for permission with vous (plural) followed by de + infinitive. Remercier takes the person as its direct object and the thing after pour: je vous remercie pour vos mots si gentils, whereas merci takes pour directly. Les retrouvailles is feminine and used only in the plural: un dîner de retrouvailles. Le verre is the everyday word for a wine glass: un verre de vin. Et vous deux, comment vous êtes-vous rencontrés ? uses the reflexive se rencontrer in the passé composé with être, so the participle agrees with vous: rencontrés for a mixed pair or two men, rencontrées for two women; the inverted form vous êtes-vous rencontrés is more formal than the spoken vous vous êtes rencontrés comment ?
lessons.scene: At a reunion dinner in a restaurant in Seville, Clara raises her glass of wine in front of her travel friends. She asks permission to say a few words, then proposes a toast to their friendship and to the hostess who prepared the table, and everyone answers: Cheers to everyone. Marco offers a toast to Clara because she always keeps the best memories of every trip, and she thanks them warmly. To keep the conversation going, Clara asks a new couple how they met. When dessert arrives, the chef comes out to say hello and the group toasts him again.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Dans un restaurant de Séville, Clara lève son verre de vin pendant le dîner de retrouvailles avec ses amis de voyage.
reader.en: At a restaurant in Seville, Clara raises her glass of wine during the reunion dinner with her travel friends.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Elle regarde tout le monde et dit : « Vous me permettez de dire quelques mots ? »
reader.en: She looks at everyone and says: May I say a few words?

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Puis elle sourit et dit : « Je voudrais porter un toast à notre amitié et à notre hôtesse, qui a dressé cette si jolie table. »
reader.en: Then she smiles and says: I would like to propose a toast to our friendship and to the hostess, who prepared this lovely table.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Tout le monde lève son verre et répond : « À la santé de tous ! »
reader.en: Everyone raises their glasses and answers: Cheers to everyone!

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Ensuite, Marco porte un toast à Clara parce qu'elle garde toujours les meilleurs souvenirs de chaque voyage.
reader.en: Afterward, Marco offers a toast to Clara because she always keeps the best memories of every trip.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Clara répond chaleureusement : « Merci beaucoup pour vos mots si gentils. »
reader.en: Clara answers warmly: Thank you so much for your kind words.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Pour continuer la conversation, elle demande à un couple qu'elle ne connaît pas encore : « Et vous deux, comment vous êtes-vous rencontrés ? »
reader.en: To keep the conversation going, she asks a new couple: And how did you two meet?

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Quand le dessert arrive, le chef sort de la cuisine pour saluer les convives et le groupe trinque de nouveau à sa santé.
reader.en: When dessert arrives, the chef comes out to say hello and the group toasts him again.

lessons.internalReviewNote: Owner-only source-pinned draft built from the travel-zone.ts Core 26 plan and Spanish lesson 26 (Un brindis entre amigos). Reader English lines copied from source passage.native in order; all 17 source word strings are the first 17 cards in source order. Factual questions for a qualified fr-FR reviewer: (1) the source anfitriona prepares the table at a restaurant in Seville, so it is unclear whether she is restaurant staff or a friend hosting; l'hôtesse is used, and maîtresse de maison would suit a private host while l'hôtesse alone can read as a restaurant greeter; (2) le verre was chosen over la coupe for a wine glass (coupe usually names a champagne or dessert glass); (3) un couple qu'elle ne connaît pas encore interprets the source new couple as new to Clara, not newly formed; (4) the chef comes out to greet diners (sort de la cuisine pour saluer les convives) and the group toasts his health. Not validated with validate:core60. Native-speaker review: test the idiom « À la santé de tous ! » and whether l'hôtesse fits the restaurant setting.
